newsitem.title: UK: OTC gold options highlight $340 strike, vols slip.
newsitem.headline: OTC gold options highlight $340 strike, vols slip.

text.p: Over-the-counter gold options expiring on Monday should keep the spot bullion price above $340, but the market will then be faced with the prospect of a bear raid, dealers said.

A few players still short of calls mainly clustered around the $340-$341 area lent support to gold this week after sentiment was whacked by the possibility of central banks activating gold reserves in the future.
But there was little enthusiasm to push gold through the $342.50 level which proved a strong cap in this week's rangebound activity.
"I don't think $335 (options strike) will come into play and I don't think $345 will come into play on Monday," said one options trader in London.
Gold's $2 range hammered implied volatilities to under 10 percent in the past week compared with about 15 percent in mid-February when spot bullion had set a new low of $336.15 an ounce.
"We have been in the $340.50-342.50 range for five straight days now. That's rather a poor performance," said one European trader.
May and June vols were trading at the 9-10 percent band and strikes were mostly confined to between $335.00-$350.00, he said.
There was interest to sell at-the-money puts with around
40-50 percent deltas. Low delta puts of around 15-20 percent were still commanding a premium of 0.50-1 percent above the at the money strikes.
"The risk reversal is in favour of the puts at the moment. That's how it has been over the last few months," said the European trader.

While gold was likely to diverge from the well-worn $340 area after Monday, it would need to reach $335 on the downside, or $350 on the upside to push volatilities back up to double-digit figures, dealers said.

Most traders expect a test of $336.15 with a possible dive to $332, although physical buyers could also be tempted below $340.00. A sudden recovery to above $345 is seen unlikely for the time being, while hot money still favours the dollar and the equity markets.
Silver's expiry will highlight the $4.70 strike, after
several attempts to break support failed as the market held comfortably around $4.72.
But traders said silver's fortunes could also be reversed after the options expiry with a possible test of the April 3 low of $4.65.
